To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a substantial proportion (44%) of MSM attending intervention sites are bisexual and this is associated with older age, reporting only penetrative behaviour with men and not receiving money for sex.

a substantial number of MSM attending Targeted Intervention sites were bisexual, with older MSM, those who reported penetrative behaviour with male partners and those who reported both penetrative and receiving anal sex being more likely to report bisexual behaviour.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and evaluation of a model of HIV/AIDS prevention for bisexual men, with particular attention to the development of a model that is appropriate for the Indian context.

the social, cultural and political factors that affect the health and well-being of men who have sex with men (MSM) and transgender women (TGW) and the impact of these on HIV transmission and prevention.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the bisexual population of MSM in India is not a hard to reach population and should be the target of HIV prevention interventions.
the HIV epidemic among men who have sex with men is a bridge epidemic to the heterosexual epidemic in India.

a significant proportion of men receiving HIV prevention services from TI programs are bisexual, the easy opportunity for reaching this population should be capitalised and focusing on older MSM as well as MSM showing penetrative behaviour with male partners may be useful to reach this population.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified a population that is likely to have a high HIV prevalence and is hard to reach, yet can be reached in the Targeted Intervention sites and can be reached through the same channels.
a large number of MSM who are at risk of HIV are likely to be reached through the Targeted Intervention programs.
the MSM epidemic is not an isolated phenomenon in India, and the HIV prevention efforts for MSM need to address the interaction between MSM and heterosexual epidemes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
MSM who pay money for sex are less likely to be involved in bisexual behaviour.
a large proportion of MSM in India are bisexual, and that they are likely to be reached through HIV intervention services for MSM.
the bisexual MSM are not a homogenous population.
